admin_intro:
This module gives you a **dock**: a small panel that shows, among your partners, **the ones that are live right now**. You see at a glance who to raid. One click on a channel copies the raid command: you just paste it in your chat. Nothing is ever sent for you.

**Your raid list lives in Contacts**: it is the cards of the “{label}” category (or the one chosen in the “Raid list” setting) that have a Twitch channel. To add or remove a partner, open their card in Contacts. You run a **community**? Put all its members there (even several thousands) and give the dock address to each of them: they have nothing to install, they just add it in OBS.
addr_steps:
1. Copy the address below.
2. In OBS, open the **Docks** menu, then **Custom Browser Docks**.
3. Type a name (for example “Raid”), paste the address, then click **Apply**.

The dock appears: put it wherever you like. You can also open the address in a tab of your browser.

**This address opens your dock to anyone who has it.** For your own use, keep it to yourself. For a community, give it to your members, and know that you can replace it at any time with “New address”: the old one then stops working for everyone. The dock never shows your notes or this address: only what Twitch already shows to everyone (name, game, title, viewers).
check_none: Everything works: nobody is live right now. Channels in your list: {n}.
renew_help: If the address was shared by mistake, or if someone should no longer have access, create a new one. The old address stops working right away for everyone, your members included: each of them will have to add the new one in OBS.
renew_confirm: Create a new address? The old one will stop working FOR EVERYONE: the dock of each person who has it will show an error until they paste the new address.
renewed: Done. The old address no longer works for anyone. Copy the new address above and give it to whoever needs it.
dock_copy_failed: Could not copy here. Select the command below and copy it (Ctrl+C).
dock_none_to_pick: Nobody to pick: none of your partners is live right now.
dock_empty: None of your partners is live right now.
dock_empty_hint: This page updates by itself. Channels in your list: {n}.
dock_no_partners: Your raid list is empty. In Contacts, add your partners' cards, with their Twitch channel, to the category of your raid list.
dock_nr_no_channel: First set up your channel in My Twitch channel: no Twitch channel is set up on your site yet.
dock_nr_channel_unknown: The channel chosen for Twitch raid is no longer one of your Twitch channels. Choose another one in the settings of Twitch raid.
dock_nr_setup: First set up the Twitch connector: the ID or the secret of your Twitch application is missing.
dock_nr_refused: Twitch refuses your site's application. In the Twitch connector, check the ID and the secret of the application.
dock_nr_outdated: The Twitch connector is too old for this module. Update it in your site's extensions.
dock_err_twitch: Twitch is not answering right now.
dock_err_rate: Twitch asks to wait a little.
dock_retry: Trying again automatically in a few seconds.
dock_denied: This address is not (or no longer) valid. Copy the dock address from the “Twitch raid” page of your site's administration.
mode_full: You have {n} channels: the dock shows all your members who are live. Above {max} channels, it offers a “Find a streamer online at random” button instead.
mode_random: You have {n} channels: the dock offers a “random” button rather than the full list. Up to {max} channels it shows every member who is live. Why? Twitch only lets us check 100 channels at a time: on a very large community, showing everyone would need far too many requests.
check_random_found: Everything works. Random test: {name} is live.
check_random_none: Everything works, but nobody was found online during this random test ({n} channels in your list). Try again in a moment.
check_partial: Careful: some channels could not be checked this time (not checked: {n}).
dock_rm_button: Find a streamer online at random
dock_rm_intro: There are many of you! Click the button to find a streamer online to raid: the command is copied for you.
dock_rm_none: Nobody was found online right now, try again.
dock_limited: Too many searches, please wait a few seconds.
dock_partial: Some channels could not be checked.
mode_full_one: You have 1 channel: the dock shows all your members who are live. Above {max} channels, it offers a “Find a streamer online at random” button instead.
list_count: **{n}** Twitch channels in the “{label}” category of Contacts.
list_count_one: **1** Twitch channel in the “{label}” category of Contacts.
list_count_awaiting: **{n}** Twitch channels: your channels from version 1, already in Contacts, waiting for their category.
list_count_awaiting_one: **1** Twitch channel: your channel from version 1, already in Contacts, waiting for its category.
list_empty: No Twitch channel in the “{label}” category yet. In Contacts, add your partners' cards to this category, with their Twitch channel.
list_only: Raid reads the “{label}” category, the only one in your Contacts. For a separate list, create the “{default}” category in Contacts: Raid will pick it up by itself.
list_moved: The chosen category was merged into “{label}”: Raid now reads that one.
list_truncated: Your list has more than {max} channels: only the first {max} are read.
contacts_stale: Contacts does not answer: the dock uses the list read at {time} (10 minutes at most). Nothing is lost.
suggest_reason: keeps your address book, where your raid list comes from
dock_nr_contacts_missing: Twitch raid reads its list in Contacts, which is not installed. Open the “Twitch raid” page of your site's administration: it offers to install it.
dock_nr_contacts_old: Contacts is not recent enough for Twitch raid. Update Contacts in the extensions of your site.
dock_nr_contacts_down: Contacts does not answer right now: the raid list cannot be read.
dock_nr_category_gone: The chosen category no longer exists, choose one in the “Raid list” setting of Twitch raid.
dock_nr_no_category: First create your raid list: in the “Raid list” setting of Twitch raid, type “{label}” then click “Create”. Then add your partners to this category in Contacts.
dock_nr_choose: Choose the Contacts category that holds your partners to raid: “Raid list” setting of Twitch raid (or create “{label}”).
mig_copy_todo: Your channels from version 1 are moving to Contacts: {done} of {total} copied. Click “Continue the copy” to finish. Nothing is lost: your version 1 list is kept as it was.
mig_copy_done: Done: your {total} channels are in Contacts.
mig_copy_partial: Copied: {done} of {total}. Click “Continue the copy” again for the rest.
mig_full: Contacts is full (100,000 cards): the copy stopped. Make room in Contacts then click “Continue the copy”.
mig_need_category: Last step: your {n} channels from version 1 are in Contacts, they need a category. In the “Settings” tab, in the “Raid list” setting, type “{label}” then click “Create”, and save. Then come back here to put your channels in it. Meanwhile, the dock keeps using these channels.
mig_finish_title: Last step: put your channels in their category
mig_finish_text: {n} cards copied from your version 1 list are not in the “{label}” category yet. The button adds them to it in Contacts: nothing is deleted, nothing is overwritten. Meanwhile, the dock already uses them.
mig_finish_btn: Put my channels in this category
mig_finish_done: Done: all your channels are in the “{label}” category.
mig_finish_partial: Partly done: {n} left. Click again to continue.
mig_skipped: {n} lines of your version 1 list were not valid Twitch names and were not copied: {list}.
mig_need_category_contacts: Last step: your {n} channels from version 1 are in Contacts, they need a category. In Contacts, create the “{label}” category, then come back here to put your channels in it. Meanwhile, the dock keeps using these channels.
